senses.sense_definition: The pursuit or exercise of the intellect; devotion to intellectual matters.

examples.text: The university atmosphere fostered a culture of vibrant <w>intellectualism</w> and intense debate.
Critics accused the politician of detached <w>intellectualism</w> that ignored ordinary working people.

senses.sense_definition: The philosophical doctrine that knowledge is derived primarily from pure reason rather than sensory experience.

examples.text: Classical <w>intellectualism</w> maintains that ultimate truth can be grasped through reason alone.
His philosophical essay contrasts radical <w>intellectualism</w> with empirical methods of inquiry.

senses.sense_definition: The practice of using mental capacity or intellect as a primary criterion of value or judgment.

examples.text: The admissions process was criticized for its rigid <w>intellectualism</w> at the expense of practical skills.
He argued against an excessive <w>intellectualism</w> that undervalues emotional intelligence.
